PullRequest.Title: sessions: stop polling the Agent Host session list when a listing fails to apply
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Opening Agents window sessions on an older remote Agent Host over SSH could freeze the connection. The client was fetching the full session list from the host once a second and never stopped.

## Root cause

`BaseAgentHostSessionsProvider._refreshSessions` retries failed refreshes with exponential backoff (1s → 30s). #319216 added this to recover from authentication races at startup. A single `catch` covered both the `listSessions()` request and applying its result. The backoff resets as soon as the request succeeds, so a listing that always fails to apply was fetched again every second.

Since #339492, `createAdapter` registers each listed session's backend identity and rejects conflicts. Hosts built before #340203 list legacy subagent rows (`copilotcli:/<id>#subagent/<toolCallId>`) whose frontend identity collides with their parent session. As a result, every refresh threw `Conflicting backend identities`, and sessions listed after the first such row never appeared. In the affected logs, the client sent about 250 `listSessions` requests (about 311 KB each) every 5 minutes to an SSH host running a 1.141 Insiders build.

## Changes

- Skip a listed session that cannot be registered and log a warning, so the rest of the listing still applies.
- Register fragment-free listed sessions before fragment rows. The frontend session key drops the fragment, so a `<parent>#subagent/<id>` row can no longer claim its parent's key by being listed first.
- Arm the backoff retry only when `listSessions()` rejects. A failure while applying a returned listing is logged and not fetched again.

#340203 already stops updated hosts from listing these rows. This change keeps the client working when it talks to an older host, and prevents any other failure while applying a listing from turning into the same poll.

## How to test

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts`: passed (725 passing, 11 pending). Both new tests fail on `main` without the fix (10 list requests in 10 s instead of 1). The listing test lists the subagent row before its parent, which fails without the ordering.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/browser/baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts`: passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/sessions/contrib/providers/**/*.test.js"`: 4 failures in `AgentHostModePicker` and `Open Agent Host State File`. The same tests also fail on `main` without this change.

Not run: a manual end-to-end check against a remote host built before #340203.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: A deterministic exception while applying an already-returned session catalog entered the network-failure retry path after the backoff had been reset, repeatedly fetching and deserializing the complete remote catalog once per second.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Opening/reconnecting an affected Agent Host could continuously transfer and deserialize the full session list at 1 Hz, consuming remote connection bandwidth and making an SSH-backed sessions window unresponsive.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The added didList flag distinguishes a rejected listSessions boundary from failure after a listing was returned. At RIGHT line 7998, post-list failures are logged and returned without arming the retry timer, while genuine connection/auth listing failures retain the exponential-backoff retry. Per-row registration conflicts are also isolated so remaining rows can reconcile.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Before this diff, one catch covered both the listSessions RPC and all synchronous reconciliation. A successful RPC reset _sessionRefreshRetryDelay to the 1s minimum at base line 7902; if createAdapter/registerBackendSession or a later reconciliation hook then threw, that same catch called _scheduleSessionRefreshRetry. The next successful full-list RPC reset the delay again before the deterministic apply failure, producing a full list request every second. The added test advances 10 seconds and requires exactly one list call for a deterministic apply failure, directly exercising the old repeated-request path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or reconnect the Sessions window to an older remote Agent Host whose full catalog contains legacy fragment subagent rows that collide with parent identities.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: setConnection immediately starts _refreshSessions; on a cold cache the listSessions round trip and catalog reconciliation must complete before the authoritative remote session list appears. Persisted summaries can render first on a warm cache, but reconciliation remains the background path that makes them authoritative.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: One Agent Host protocol listSessions request returns and deserializes the complete remote session catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full-catalog request for the connection attempt after the diff. Before the diff, a deterministic registration/apply exception scheduled another request at the reset 1-second minimum, so cost grew with connection lifetime until the failure disappeared.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The boundary already existed, but successful listing followed by an apply exception entered the retry path and repeated the complete request every second.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The first request is on the cold session-list critical path; erroneous retries consumed the same SSH/network connection and repeatedly parsed the catalog after the UI could not complete reconciliation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N returned host sessions, including legacy subagent rows. The diff clones and sorts N entries in O(N log N), then performs the existing O(N) reconciliation; one operation serves the whole host and there is no per-session IPC fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: _ensureSessionCache suppresses a second refresh while one request is in flight or a retry timer is armed. Direct refresh triggers use generations so only the newest response applies; the diff adds no concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold cache creates adapters for valid rows. A warm persisted cache contains at most 100 summaries and updates existing adapters, while the live host listing itself is not capped. Failed registrations are not negatively cached, so a later explicit refresh retries them, but the diff no longer creates a timer-driven poll after the successful list response.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the single full-list protocol request, 1-second reset/retry loop before the fix, and post-list no-retry gate are directly traced in code and tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Live catalog size and SSH latency vary. The added sort/allocation is real but comparator work is small relative to already-required full-catalog transfer, parsing, and reconciliation, so it does not establish a user-visible regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change removes repeated full-catalog network work; parent-first ordering and per-row isolation add only bounded in-process work without additional boundary calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Local Agent Host startup when authentication is unsettled or listSessions transiently rejects.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After authenticationPending settles, the provider eagerly requests the catalog so the sidebar can populate. A rejected request leaves the cache non-authoritative and the exponential-backoff retry is required for startup recovery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Agent Host protocol listSessions request to the local Agent Host process, including full-catalog serialization and client-side URI/metadata mapping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial request; genuine rejection retries at 1s, 2s, 4s up to 30s until success. This behavior is unchanged. A successful response that later fails to apply now makes no automatic retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same IPC request and exponential backoff existed, but apply failures were incorrectly classified as request failures and repeatedly reset to the minimum delay.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The first successful request is required for an authoritative cold startup catalog; backoff retries are delayed recovery work after failure.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N local sessions in one catalog. Ordering adds one N-element array and O(N log N) cheap fragment comparisons before the existing adapter/update pass.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The in-flight and pending-retry guards coalesce synchronous getSessions calls. One disposable timer owns backoff; no changed parallel IPC fan-out occurs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Up to 100 persisted summaries may render immediately on warm startup. Empty success is authoritative and resets backoff; rejection remains distinct and retried. The change preserves those positive, empty, and failure states.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor/auth autorun trigger, local protocol boundary, retry state, and tests for first-failure recovery are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The local catalog is uncapped at the protocol boundary, but no evidence shows the added in-memory sort dominates the pre-existing full protocol mapping and reconciliation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. Genuine startup failures still recover with bounded backoff, while deterministic post-response failures stop generating repeated IPC.

Scenarios.Scenario: A chat turn completes or a newly committed session waits for reconciliation.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ChatTurnComplete starts a background refresh and is off the immediate action-dispatch critical path. _waitForNewSession explicitly awaits refresh, so its one catalog request and reconciliation are on the path to resolving the committed session.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: One full listSessions protocol request for the connected host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One host-wide request per completion/wait trigger, not one per session. This pre-existing cardinality is unchanged by the diff; generation checks prevent stale responses from applying.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same triggers issued the same full-list request. The diff only orders the returned array and changes retry classification after a response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background for ordinary turn completion; blocking for _waitForNewSession until the returned catalog is reconciled.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N sessions per host catalog and event frequency. Added CPU is O(N log N) per pre-existing explicit refresh, with no new request multiplicity.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Refresh generations make the latest invocation authoritative; this change neither adds Promise.all fan-out nor increases aggregate request scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm adapters are updated instead of recreated. Failed colliding rows are attempted on each explicit refresh because they are not cached; that is bounded by existing refresh events rather than a new timer.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for trigger and boundary cardinality; low evidence of any measurable regression from the added ordering alone.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Frequent turns and unusually large catalogs increase sorting/logging work, but the diff simultaneously eliminates the much larger 1 Hz failure loop and does not add a trigger or expensive boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression because request frequency is unchanged on healthy explicit-refresh paths and deterministic apply failures now avoid automatic polling.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced remote connection, local startup, explicit turn refresh, and new-session wait paths through their full-catalog protocol boundaries. No performance finding was introduced. Recorded the PR as a high-confidence fix for the prior 1 Hz repeated full-list regression introduced by commit 4918ed64f11c8fb78f89b7c40805c1ddab82790b.
